title: Instant Pot Pulled Pork
description: Bone-in Prairie Fresh pork shoulder (6.5 to 10 lb), pressure cooked (or slow cooked) and shredded. Makes enough for about 4 to 6 meals.

ingredients.note: or mix: 1 Tbsp salt, 1 Tbsp paprika, 2 tsp garlic powder, 2 tsp dried minced onion, 1 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp chili powder (optional: drizzle of maple syrup)

steps: Cut to fit. Cut the meat into 3 to 5 large chunks (about 2 lb each), cutting around the bone. Trim the thickest outside fat cap if you like. Put the bone in the pot too, it adds flavor. Don't fill past the 2/3 line. If it won't all fit, cook in two batches or use the slow cook method.
Season. Pat dry and rub all over with the rub.
Sear (optional, adds flavor). Saute mode, oil, brown the chunks 2 to 3 min per side in batches. Remove the meat.
Liquid. Add the water and Better Than Bouillon. Scrape the bottom so nothing is stuck (this prevents the "Burn" warning). Put the trivet in if you have it, then the pork.
Pressure cook on High: 60 to 75 min for 2 lb chunks. If cooking a bigger whole-ish piece (4 lb+), go 90 to 100 min.
Natural release at least 15 to 20 min, then release the rest.
Check. It should pull apart easily with a fork (about 195 to 205°F). If it fights you, pressure cook 10 to 15 more min.
Shred. Pull out the meat, remove bone and big fat pieces, shred with 2 forks. Skim fat off the liquid and stir a ladle or two of the juice back into the meat so it stays moist.
source: Joe's Meal Pack, Oct 20 to Nov 4, 2026 (built by Thrifty, now kept by Meal Plan), R3
notes:
Hands-on 20 min. Total about 2 to 2.5 hours (pressure) or 8 to 10 hours (slow cook).
Slow cook alternative: same prep. Slow Cook mode, lid on (vent can stay on venting), Low 8 to 10 hours or High 5 to 6 hours, until fork-tender. Shred the same way.
Storage: fridge 3 to 4 days. Freeze in meal-size bags with a little juice, flat, labeled, up to 2 to 3 months.

healthy: Pork shoulder is high in protein.
Pressure cooked in water with only 1 Tbsp oil.
not_healthy: Pork shoulder is a fatty cut with saturated fat.
Dry rub and bouillon base add sodium.
BBQ sauce adds sugar and sodium.
